strategy.summary: Reproduce the ARDL↔UECM residual mismatch by fitting an ARDL model and its equivalent UECM created via `UECM.from_ardl` (or equivalent constructor params as in the project test), then asserting that `uecm_res.resid` equals `ardl_res.resid`. The buggy revision fails this equality because UECM residuals are computed using UECM fitted values in differences subtracted from the ARDL endogenous data in levels; the fixed revision overrides `resid` to use `model._y - self.fittedvalues` so that UECM residuals match ARDL residuals.

pinned_because: Pin statsmodels to the exact buggy and fixed revisions that contain/resolve PR #9390; the behaviour is in the library code (`statsmodels/tsa/ardl/model.py`) and is not guaranteed across releases.

strategy.reproducing_test: Run the project’s own test `test_resids_ardl_uecm` (added in the PR diff). It fits an ARDL and a UECM with the same data and orders, then asserts `assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)`.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (commit d0da572b061f), the assertion `assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)` fails because UECM residuals are computed inconsistently with ARDL residuals (differences-vs-levels mismatch). On the fixed revision (the commit produced by PR #9390, where `resid` is overridden as described), the same assertion passes because UECM residuals match ARDL residuals.
strategy.numerical_probe: Not a separately checked number: rely solely on the test’s internal `assert_allclose` comparison of entire residual arrays (`uecm_res.resid` vs `ardl_res.resid`).

input_output_examples.input: Fit ARDL and UECM on `dane_data` using the same lags/orders/spec: `ardl_mod = ARDL(dane_data.lrm, 3, dane_data[["lry","ibo","ide"]], {"lry":1,"ibo":3,"ide":2}); ardl_res = ardl_mod.fit(); uecm_mod = UECM(dane_data.lrm, 3, dane_data[["lry","ibo","ide"]], {"lry":1,"ibo":3,"ide":2}); uecm_res = uecm_mod.fit();` then compare `uecm_res.resid` to `ardl_res.resid`.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Residual arrays differ, so `assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)` raises an assertion failure.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Residual arrays match closely enough for `assert_allclose` to succeed.

risks: The reproduction assumes the exact test data fixture `dane_data` and ARDL/UECM model API behave as in the repository containing this test; if `dane_data` fixture changes across versions, results may not transition.

This strategy does not assume a specific floating-point tolerance beyond what `assert_allclose` uses in the project’s test environment; if CI uses unusual NumPy settings (e.g., single precision or altered tolerances), the failure/passing boundary could shift.

If the defect only appears when `UECM` is created via `UECM.from_ardl(ardl)` (as described in issue #9323) rather than via the explicit `UECM(...)` constructor used in the added test, then using only `test_resids_ardl_uecm` may not fail on the buggy revision. To mitigate: also run/implement an additional check mirroring issue #9323: `uecm = UECM.from_ardl(ardl_mod); uecm_res = uecm.fit(); assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)`.

Platform/toolchain variability risk is low because the bug is a logical mismatch in model residual computation, not a hardware-specific numerical issue; however it still depends on linear algebra backend (BLAS/LAPACK) for close agreement.

oracle.reference_source: Project-added test equality: `assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)` asserts that residuals from UECM and equivalent ARDL match.
oracle.why: The correctness requirement stated in issue #9323 and implemented in PR #9390 is that UECM derived from an ARDL should have the same residuals as the ARDL because no residual transformation is made during derivation. The provided PR test codifies this as an all-close comparison of the full residual arrays.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: `assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)` fails due to residual computation mixing UECM fitted values (computed in differences) with ARDL endogenous data (in levels), producing incorrect UECM residuals (as described in issue #9323 and PR #9390).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: `assert_allclose(uecm_res.resid, ardl_res.resid)` passes because the fixed code overrides the UECM `resid` computation to use `model._y - self.fittedvalues`, aligning residuals with the ARDL residuals.
